course.title: International Integrated Science 9
course.subtitle: Life, Matter, Energy and Earth Systems
course.credit_recommendation: 1 high-school science credit, subject to local law and school policy
course.mapping_status: International benchmark synthesis. Jurisdiction-specific review is required before formal standards or credit reporting.
course.assessment_principle: Every scored item must have one definitive, defensible answer or an explicit evidence-based rubric.
course.current_release: Unit 00 — Readiness, Laboratory Safety & Scientific Habits

mastery_scale.label: Beginning
mastery_scale.description: Needs direct instruction, modeling, and supported practice.

mastery_scale.label: Developing
mastery_scale.description: Shows partial understanding with inconsistent application or evidence.

mastery_scale.label: Proficient
mastery_scale.description: Applies scientific ideas and practices accurately in familiar contexts.

mastery_scale.label: Mastered
mastery_scale.description: Explains, transfers, evaluates, and applies learning in unfamiliar contexts.

units.title: Readiness, Laboratory Safety & Scientific Habits
units.big_idea: Safe, ethical, careful scientific work begins with habits that protect people, evidence, organisms, communities, and environments.
objectives: Complete a non-punitive science readiness diagnostic
Apply laboratory, field, digital, and household investigation safety rules
Distinguish observations, inferences, hypotheses, models, theories, and laws
Use SI units, significant figures at an introductory level, and organized science records
Set a personal scientific inquiry goal
framework_tags: Universal: Nature and Practices of Science
IB MYP Sciences: Inquiring and designing

units.title: Scientific Inquiry, Measurement & Evidence
units.big_idea: Scientific explanations become stronger when questions are testable, measurements are reliable, and claims are supported by transparent evidence.
objectives: Formulate testable questions and defensible hypotheses
Identify independent, dependent, and controlled variables
Plan fair tests and observational studies
Collect, graph, analyze, and evaluate quantitative and qualitative data
Identify uncertainty, anomalies, limitations, correlation, and causation
Construct claim-evidence-reasoning explanations
framework_tags: NGSS: Planning investigations; analyzing data; argument from evidence
IB MYP Sciences: Criteria B and C
PISA: Evaluate scientific inquiry and interpret evidence

units.title: Cells & the Organization of Life
units.big_idea: Cells are organized systems whose structures and processes make life possible across many scales.
objectives: Apply cell theory and compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
Relate organelle structures to functions
Model diffusion, osmosis, and membrane transport
Explain how cells form tissues, organs, and organ systems
Use microscopy or virtual microscopy to gather evidence
Evaluate the limits of cell models
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Cells and systems
Cambridge Biology: Characteristics and organization of organisms
British Columbia Science 9: Cells and reproduction

units.title: Body Systems & Homeostasis
units.big_idea: Organ systems interact through feedback and transport processes to maintain stable internal conditions.
objectives: Explain interactions among major human body systems
Model negative feedback and homeostasis
Analyze heart rate, breathing, recovery, or other safe physiological data
Connect nutrition, respiration, circulation, and cellular energy
Evaluate health claims using credible scientific evidence
Discuss biological variation without treating difference as deficiency
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Systems and interactions
Cambridge Biology: Human nutrition, transport, respiration, coordination

units.title: Cell Division, Reproduction & Inheritance
units.big_idea: Genetic information is copied, expressed, reshuffled, and inherited, producing both continuity and variation.
objectives: Compare mitosis and meiosis
Explain sexual and asexual reproduction
Model chromosomes, genes, alleles, genotype, and phenotype
Use probability models for introductory inheritance
Connect mutation and recombination to variation
Examine ethical questions in genetics using evidence and respectful reasoning
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Genetics and ethics
NGSS: Inheritance and variation of traits

units.title: Ecosystems, Evolution & Biodiversity
units.big_idea: Living populations change over time and depend on interconnected flows of energy, matter, information, and environmental conditions.
objectives: Model food webs, trophic levels, and energy transfer
Explain population limits, niches, competition, and symbiosis
Describe natural selection using evidence
Connect adaptation, variation, and biodiversity
Conduct a local or digital ecosystem investigation
Evaluate human impacts and conservation trade-offs
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Environments and consequences
NGSS: Ecosystems; natural selection and evolution

units.title: Atomic Structure & Periodic Patterns
units.big_idea: The arrangement and behavior of subatomic particles explain patterns in elements, isotopes, ions, and materials.
objectives: Model protons, neutrons, electrons, atoms, ions, and isotopes
Use atomic number and mass number
Interpret introductory electron arrangements
Explain major periodic table patterns
Distinguish elements, compounds, and mixtures
Describe introductory nuclear change and radiation safety
framework_tags: Cambridge Chemistry: Particulate nature and atomic structure
NGSS: Structure and properties of matter

units.title: Bonding, Chemical Reactions & Matter
units.big_idea: Atoms rearrange during chemical reactions while matter and charge are conserved.
objectives: Compare ionic and covalent bonding at an introductory level
Interpret chemical formulas and particle diagrams
Identify evidence of chemical change
Represent and balance simple chemical equations
Apply conservation of mass
Investigate reaction rate, acids and bases, or material properties safely
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Reactions and consequences
Cambridge Chemistry: Bonding, equations, acids and bases

units.title: Motion, Forces & Energy
units.big_idea: Changes in motion and energy can be measured, modeled, predicted, and engineered.
objectives: Calculate and interpret speed and introductory acceleration
Use motion graphs
Model balanced and unbalanced forces
Apply Newtonian ideas qualitatively and quantitatively at an introductory level
Distinguish kinetic, potential, thermal, and other energy stores and transfers
Analyze efficiency and conservation of energy
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Movement and energy
Cambridge Physics: Motion, forces, and energy

units.title: Electricity, Waves & Information
units.big_idea: Electrical and wave systems transfer energy and information through patterns that can be measured and controlled.
objectives: Construct and compare safe series and parallel circuits
Measure or simulate current, voltage, and resistance
Apply introductory circuit relationships
Describe amplitude, frequency, wavelength, reflection, and refraction
Compare sound, light, and electromagnetic communication
Evaluate benefits, limitations, and safety considerations of communication technologies
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Energy transfer and communication

units.title: Earth Systems & Biogeochemical Cycles
units.big_idea: Earth functions through interacting geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and cryosphere systems.
objectives: Model interactions among Earth's major spheres
Trace water, carbon, nitrogen, and rock cycles
Analyze energy flow through Earth systems
Interpret maps, satellite images, and public environmental datasets
Explain feedback, equilibrium, and system change
Connect local observations to regional and global systems
framework_tags: British Columbia Science 9: Earth spheres and cycles

units.title: Dynamic Earth, Climate & Space
units.big_idea: Evidence from rocks, hazards, climate records, planetary motion, and light reveals a changing Earth within a larger universe.
objectives: Interpret geologic time and evidence of Earth's history
Explain plate tectonics and natural hazards
Differentiate weather, climate, variability, and long-term change
Analyze multiple lines of climate evidence
Model solar system motion and scale
Use light and gravity as evidence in introductory astronomy
framework_tags: Universal: Earth, climate, and space science
IB MYP Sciences: Global and cosmic systems
PISA: Environmental evidence and informed action

units.title: Sustainable Engineering Capstone
units.big_idea: Engineering uses scientific evidence, criteria, constraints, testing, and revision to improve solutions while accounting for human and environmental consequences.
objectives: Define a meaningful local or global problem
Establish measurable criteria and constraints
Research scientific background and existing solutions
Design, model, test, and revise a solution
Evaluate safety, cost, accessibility, culture, reliability, and environmental effects
Present evidence, limitations, and recommendations to a public audience
framework_tags: IB MYP Sciences: Impacts of science
